from collections import Counter
# one-copy token inventory recovered by dividing all counts by four
raw='''1.:1 2.:1 3.:1 4.:1 5.:1 6.:1 =:3 After:1 COLOR:1 COLOR.:1 COLOR;:2 Do:1 Initially,:1 Move:3 Perform:1 Replace:1 Reply:1 Swap:3 You:1 add:1 all:1 and:5 any:1 below.:1 blue:3 blue,:1 box:7 boxes:2 boxes.:2 brass:4 coin:2 coin,:1 coin.:1 completing:1 containing:3 contains:3 contents:2 currently:1 each:2 entire:2 exactly:1 final:1 format::1 glass:3 green:3 green.:1 have:1 in:2 into:3 key:2 key,:1 key.:1 label:1 label.:1 labeled:2 labels:1 line:1 marble:2 marble.:1 moving:1 not:1 numbered:1 object.:1 objects.:1 of:3 on:1 one:1 operations:1 operations,:1 order:1 other:1 red:3 red,:1 red.:1 report:1 shown:1 silver:4 six:2 text.:1 the:25 this:1 three:1 visible:2 with:2 without:1'''
c=Counter()
for item in raw.split():
    w,n=item.rsplit(':',1); c[w]=int(n)
fixed='''You have six labeled boxes and three objects. Initially, the red box contains the silver coin, the blue box contains the brass key, and the green box contains the glass marble. Perform the six operations in the numbered order shown below. After completing all six operations, report the final visible label on the box containing each object. Reply with exactly one line in this format: silver = COLOR; brass = COLOR; glass = COLOR. Replace each COLOR with the visible label. Do not add any other text.'''.split()
c.subtract(fixed)
print('negative', {k:v for k,v in c.items() if v<0})
print('remaining',sum(c.values()))
print(' '.join(f'{k}*{v}' if v"'!=1 else k for k,v in c.items() if v>0))
PY'
